description: A Permata Bank corporate account registered as a CV (Commanditaire Vennootschap) importing textile goods received large SWIFT remittances from Hong Kong and Singapore totaling the equivalent of IDR 4,200,000,000 over 6 weeks. However, import documentation submitted to the bank showed invoiced goods worth only IDR 890,000,000, indicating significant trade-based money laundering (TBML) via over-invoicing. The excess funds, approximately IDR 3,310,000,000, were distributed via RTGS to a network of 8 supplier accounts, several of which were linked to a narcotics trafficking syndicate under investigation by BNN (Badan Narkotika Nasional). The CV had been incorporated only 4 months prior and had no prior import/export history. Bank Indonesia's SLIK check showed no credit history for the directors.
